groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
W: Welcome to Money Matters, a weekly program that helps you manage your money. Tonight, I'll be talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting.
M: Hello, everyone.
W: There's a magic about money. When it's not planned for, tracked and kept a record of, it literally disappears. What are some of the steps we can take to prevent this from happening?
M: Well, it's all about keeping track of your money. If you don't do that, you'll never be able to set any goals for your budget or have the discipline to stick to them.
W: That's easier said than done. I read recently that only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget.
M: Yes, but knowing what you earn and what you spend can give you reassurance that you won't get into debt in the first place. You can do this by adding up all of your sources of income you have and writing them all down on a piece of paper. On the same page, write down all of your monthly expenses.
W: I'm always amazed at how much my expenses add up. But designating each item as an income or an expense really helps me have a much better sense of all my spending.
M: Right, most people have no idea how much they spend each day, let alone each week or month, no matter how careful they are. Next, subtract your monthly expenses from income. If the result is positive, you are living within your means. If the result is a negative number, you're going to have to cut back on your spending.
W: I'm usually a negative number. I just can't resist the allure of all those prestigious goods.
M: Well, it's not a catastrophe. But you do have to make some changes. Try cutting back on those non-essential items, sell some stuff in your attic, or shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations like chocolate. Failing that you can always find yourself a part-time job.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
M: Hi there, I've come to see the flat. My name is Mark Adams. We spoke on the phone on Wednesday.
W: Hi, Mark, come on up. I'll buzz you in. Green door on the second floor on the right side. Nice to meet you, I spoke to all your references and they all checked out okay. So let me show you around. The place actually belongs to my mother, but her health isn't great, so we finally managed to persuade her to move in with us and rent this old place out.
M: It's a great size. Plenty of space. Very versatile. I think it's a winner for us.
W: Yes, all the appliances are brand-new. There's a washing machine and a tumble dryer in the utility room next to the kitchen.
M: Lots of closet space too, which is fabulous. My wife has a ridiculous number of shoes. Now, the big question: What about noise and the neighbours?
W: Well, all the neighbours are elderly, so no noisy kids. And the back of the house overlooks a clear and peaceful pond, so it's perfect if tranquility is what you are looking for.
M: That's good news. We've been living in a less than glamorous part of Aberdeen, constantly harassed day and night by noisy neighbours. Getting to work was a nightmare too, as we only have one car and my wife has to use it as she works nights at the hospital.
W: Well, if you like the place, it's yours, as soon as I get a contract drawn up with the solicitor. The first month's rent and a deposit are mandatory on signing the contract. Then we can work out when is the best day for you to pay rent each month.
M: We'll be incredibly happy to be your new tenants. Thank you so much, My wife will be thrilled to get out of the shabby place we are now in, and start filling those wardrobes with all those shoes.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
A new study has found a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels. Why? Because the more television kids watch, the more they're exposed to advertising. The more advertising they see, the more likely they are to insist on purchasing items when they go with their parents to the store. This could generate conflict if the parents refuse. All that, researchers say, can contribute to parents' overall stress levels.
What's the solution? Perhaps the most obvious is curtailing screen time. Commercial content is there for a reason: to elicit purchasing behavior. So parents might want to shut off the TV. Researchers concede that this is easier said than done. So they suggest another option. Parents can change how they talk to their kids about purchases.
The researchers suggest that parents seek input from their children on family purchasing decisions. They shouldn't try to control all purchases. Instead, parents might tell their children things like "I will listen to your advice on certain products or brands." This type of communication, the researchers assert, can lead to children making fewer purchasing demands. That means less parents' stress.
However, the protective effect of this kind of communication diminishes with greater exposure to television. This is because advertising aimed at children is especially persuasive. Advertisers use an assortment of tactics, such as bright colors, happy music and celebrity endorsements to appeal to children. Plus, children don't have the cognitive ability to fully understand advertising's intent. That makes them particularly vulnerable to advertisements.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
Everyone is supposed to cheer for good guys, and we should only punish the bad guys. But that's not what we always do. Most of the time, we do indeed reward good people. We also often punish people who harm others, or who aren't good team players. But sometimes, the good guys also get punished or criticized, specifically because they are so good.
This seems baffling, because it's detrimental to group cooperation. However, the phenomenon has been discovered in multiple fields, and it has been found in every society. Why does this happen? Research suggests a simple reason. When one person looks really good, others look bad by comparison. Those others then have an incentive in stopping that person from looking good, especially if they can't or won't compete. After all, we're all judged in comparison with others.
When faced with someone better, what can a normal person do? One option is to actively compete. A second option is to bring that person down; that is, to suppress their cooperation or work ethic, infer selfish motives for their actions, or imply real or imagined hypocrisy. Other tactics include attacking them on unrelated dimensions, or punishing them outright.
Why does this matter? Critics often attack the motives of people who protect the environment, donate money, or work too hard. Such good deeds are dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds. This criticism may ultimately discourage people from doing good deeds. So it's important to recognize these attacks for what they are.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
In America, most researchers concede that boys and girls are brought up in different ways, taught different skills and rewarded for different acts. Women, it is agreed, excel at certain tasks, men at others. There's little argument that some personality traits appear more dominant in one sex than in the other. All of this notwithstanding, gender differences are very much in the media these days. Since the rise of the women's movement, gender role behavior has come under closer scrutiny. How has this affected friendship? How do the sexes differ in their friendship relations?
Most preteen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age. Both sexes share an essentially positive recollection of these childhood friendships; they do not differ in this respect. However, the type of play engaged in during these early friendships is telling of the difference to come. Boys tend to form play groups that are competitive in nature; girls' groups more frequently revolve around cooperative enterprises. Thus, at an early age, boys become concerned with trying hard and winning while girls, by contrast, play house and school, engaging in roles that require complementary support.
Speaking of their childhood, men recall being highly responsive to and aware of the gender-role opinions of other boys. Girls in preteen years appear to be less susceptible to gender-role pressure. It is not until the dating years that women report being concerned with feminine behavior. Males, for the most part, are responsive to the suggestion that their behavior is unmanly at almost any age.
These early attitudes, reinforced by social conditioning, continue to play an active part in the friendships of both sexes during adolescence. This is a period when the majority of males once again report a close alliance with same-sex friends. Now, however, with heightened intensity, considerable energy is devoted to competing for position and a definite undercurrent of competition permeates the relationship. Although in dissimilar fashion, females share equally fragile relationships at this age. For them, the bond of loyalty extends only to the line of romantic involvement. This is most apt to be the case in late adolescence, when dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood. Actually, dating dilutes the intensity of same sex friendships for men also. For the majority of us, the moment we begin to date seriously, there's a competition between romance and friendship.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
Good afternoon. In today's lecture, we'll be talking about how and when to disclose a disability when applying for a job. On average, about 20% of the population has some form of disability. Most countries these days have equal opportunity and non-discrimination laws. Yet, disabled people often find it hard to decide when, how, and if at all to raise their disability problem with the potential employer. There is uncertainty about how a recruiter will perceive their disability.
As such, many candidates fear they wouldn't be considered for a position, as a result of disclosing this personal information. And research has validated this as a genuine concern for many job applicants. It's a natural reaction, but it shouldn't be a reason to stay quiet. People need to remember that they are applying for a position they have the skills and experience to excel in. Discussing a disability with the potential employer may help them make reasonable workplace adjustments in their favor.
It's most appropriate to discuss a disability when they reply to confirm an interview. This information needn't be put up front in their cover letter or resumé, because it's probably not relevant to the position itself. Candidates with disabilities should feel they have the power to make their own decisions around sharing this information free from prejudice. If they find an organization that doesn't celebrate diversity and inclusion, it could say a lot about the company's culture. Perhaps the organization isn't the right fit. It's important for them to remember that they are seeking a manager and employer that's going to be supportive and continue to give them a great employment experience.
Companies sometimes offer candidates the chance to disclose disabilities on their application form, but people shouldn't feel restricted by this method or timing. People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition. There is always the risk that the recruiter will research information that is inaccurate or irrelevant. If people don't think their disability will impact their ability to perform in the advertised position, then it's entirely their entitlement to choose when, and whether to share this information.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Smartphones distract attention and reduce learning because of their potential to offer activities more inviting than study. But what about background sound alone?
A group of American researchers compared students' comprehension of verbal material when reading in the presence of background speech, instrumental music or general noise. General noise is neutral, such as that from the sound of an air conditioner or fan. Students' scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech. Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music than with speech. However, when they were asked to identify melodies rather than understand text, background music interfered more. When the background speech was in a language unfamiliar to participants, there was little if any hindrance of reading comprehension.
British researchers compared the effects of background speech, vocal music, instrumental music, general background noise and silence on short-term memory. Background speech had the biggest negative effect; vocal music was slightly more disruptive than instrumental; and general background noise and silence were least disruptive. It seems the degree of interference from background noise depends on the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise.
The studies suggest that when people read and when they try to remember any verbal material, background speech will inhibit their ability. Instrumental music will have at worst a slight effect. When students write essays, however, other research has found it is best to reduce all background noise as much as possible.
Not everyone reacts in the same way to distractions. Other studies suggest some aspects of personality may make a difference. The researchers subjected shy quiet people and confident outgoing ones to high arousal or low arousal background music, general noise or silence while asking them to remember words. Everyone performed best in the silent condition, but less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions. So when children are reading and trying to incorporate new material, parents could consider allowing some background music, particularly if it's instrumental and their child is the outgoing type.

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the weekly program?
options: It enables people to earn more money.
It teaches the importance of financing.
It helps people with budgeting.
It introduces a novel way to invest.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about the weekly program? 

 【翻译】 男士对这个每周节目有何评价? 
 A)  它能让人们赚更多钱。 
 B)  它教授理财的重要性。 
 C)  它帮助人们做预算。 
 D)  它介绍了一种新颖的投资方式。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It helps people with budgeting. 
 【定位】 P1 Welcome to Money Matters, a weekly program that helps you manage your money. Tonight, I'll be talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting. 
 欢迎收听《金钱要事》，这是一档帮你管理钱财的每周节目。今晚，我将和玛丽·约翰逊聊聊预算的话题。 

 【信号】 开场点题句 。节目开头的自我介绍 a weekly program that helps you manage your money 加上 talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting，是典型的"开场点题"信号——节目类录音常在第一两句报出自己是干嘛的，这句就是定位锚。 

 【替换】 talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting ↔ helps people with budgeting 原词budgeting+功能补全 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 录音说节目"helps you manage your money"（帮你管钱），不是帮你"earn more money"（赚更多钱）；管钱 ≠ 赚钱，方向被偷换。  借用原文：helps you manage your money 

 B) 未提及 录音谈的是 budgeting（预算/记账），并没说节目"teaches the importance of financing"（讲融资/理财的重要性）；financing 与 budgeting 是相近理财词，盗用相近概念来诱选，原文未提"重要性"这一说法。 
 D) 原词陷阱 选项 introduces a novel way to invest 借"理财"氛围里的 invest 来诱选，但录音全程讲预算与记账，从未介绍"新的投资方式"，是听到理财就联想投资的陷阱。

questions.prompt: What did the man read recently?
options: Many Americans are not satisfied with their income.
Many Americans have no idea about how to invest.
Most Americans do not know how to save money.
Most Americans do not stick to a budget.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the man read recently? 

 【翻译】 男士最近读到了什么? 
 A)  许多美国人对自己的收入不满意。 
 B)  许多美国人不知道如何投资。 
 C)  大多数美国人不知道如何省钱。 
 D)  大多数美国人不坚持预算。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Most Americans do not stick to a budget. 
 【定位】 P5 That's easier said than done. I read recently that only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget. 
 说起来容易做起来难。我最近读到，只有 41% 的美国人会坚持执行预算。 

 【信号】 I read recently 引出句 。I read recently that only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget 由"I read recently that…"直接引出"读到的内容"，是答案句的明确信号——"读到了什么"的答案就跟在该信号之后。 

 【替换】 only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget ↔ Most Americans do not stick to a budget. 肯否转换+量词换算 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音这处只说"坚持预算的比例低"，没提美国人"not satisfied with their income"（对收入不满）；满意度是另起的话题，原文未涉及。 
 B) 原词陷阱 no idea about how to invest 借理财氛围里的 invest 诱选，但这句数据讲的是"坚持预算"，与"会不会投资"无关，是听到理财词就联想的陷阱。 
 C) 偷换概念 do not know how to save money 把原文的"坚持预算（budget）"偷换成"不会存钱（save）"；后文虽另有 most people have no idea how much they spend，但那是"不清楚花了多少"，不等于"不会存钱"，且本题要的是"读到的那条"，对应的是 41% 那句。  借用原文：adhere to a budget

questions.prompt: What does the woman suggest the man do first to avoid getting into debt?
options: Keep track of his money.
Live within his means.
Find more sources of income.
Refrain from buying luxuries.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman suggest the man do first to avoid getting into debt? 

 【翻译】 女士建议男士首先做什么来避免负债? 
 A)  记录他的钱款。 
 B)  量入为出。 
 C)  寻找更多收入来源。 
 D)  克制购买奢侈品。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Keep track of his money. 
 【定位】 P4 Well, it's all about keeping track of your money. If you don't do that, you'll never be able to set any goals for your budget or have the discipline to stick to them. 
 嗯，关键全在于记录你的钱。如果你不这么做，就永远没法为预算设定目标，也没有自律去坚持它们。 

 【信号】 it's all about 强调首要 。it's all about keeping track of your money 用"it's all about…"强调"一切的根本在于"，是把某动作点为"首要/第一步"的信号；后接 If you don't do that… 进一步坐实它是前提，故这是"先做什么"的答案句。 

 【替换】 keeping track of your money ↔ Keep track of his money. near原词+人称转换 

 【排除】 B) 答非所问 Live within his means. 对应原文 If the result is positive, you are living within your means.，那是"记账并做收支相减之后"才谈到的结果，不是题目要的"first（第一步）"；盗用 living within your means 原词，却答非"先做什么"。  借用原文：living within your means 

 C) 原词陷阱 Find more sources of income. 沾原文 adding up all of your sources of income 与 find yourself a part-time job 的边，但"找更多收入来源"在录音里是 Failing that（实在不行）的最后一招，绝非"第一步"。  借用原文：sources of income 

 D) 答非所问 Refrain from buying luxuries. 对应原文 cutting back on those non-essential items，属"算出是负数后"要做的调整，同样不是"第一步"；它答非题目限定的 first。  借用原文：cutting back on those non-essential items

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about online shopping?
options: It offers a greater variety of items.
It helps avoid unnecessary spending.
It changes one's way of living.
It saves one's time for shopping.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about online shopping? 

 【翻译】 女士对网上购物有何评价? 
 A)  它提供更多种类的商品。 
 B)  它有助于避免不必要的开支。 
 C)  它改变人们的生活方式。 
 D)  它节省购物时间。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It helps avoid unnecessary spending. 
 【定位】 P10 Try cutting back on those non-essential items, sell some stuff in your attic, or shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations like chocolate. 
 试着削减那些非必需品，把阁楼里的一些东西卖掉，或者网上购物以避开像巧克力那样不必要的诱惑。 

 【信号】 shop online to avoid 目的状语 。shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations 里 to avoid 是"网购为了避开…"的目的状语，直接点出网购的好处所在，是本题答案信号——好处就藏在 to 后面那一段。 

 【替换】 shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations like chocolate ↔ It helps avoid unnecessary spending. 诱惑→花销的概括等值 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音只说网购能"避开诱惑"，没说它 offers a greater variety of items（商品更多样）；"商品多"是网购的生活常识，但本句原文没这么说。 
 C) 过度推断 It changes one's way of living. 把"避开一次诱惑"夸成"改变生活方式"，原文 shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations 远没到"改变生活方式"的程度，是过度拔高。 
 D) 原词陷阱 It saves one's time for shopping. 借"shopping"原词与网购"省时"的常识诱选，但录音说的是"避开诱惑"，从未提网购"省时间"，是听到 shop/online 就联想常识的陷阱。  借用原文：shop online

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about the flat?
options: It is brand-new.
It has plenty of rooms.
It belongs to her mother.
It has been vacant for months.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about the flat? 

 【翻译】 女士对这套公寓是怎么说的? 
 A)  它是全新的。 
 B)  它有很多房间。 
 C)  它属于她母亲。 
 D)  它已经空置好几个月了。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It belongs to her mother. 
 【定位】 P2 The place actually belongs to my mother, but her health isn't great, so we finally managed to persuade her to move in with us and rent this old place out. 
 这地方其实是我母亲的，但她身体不太好，所以我们好不容易才说服她搬来跟我们一起住，把这所老房子租出去。 

 【信号】 女方亲口陈述归属，是直接应答型答案句 。答案落在女方介绍房子时的第一句陈述 The place actually belongs to my mother，"actually"带出的正是她要交代的房子归属事实，属"被介绍方亲口给出"的直接信号。 

 【替换】 The place actually belongs to my mother ↔ It belongs to her mother 几乎原句对位，仅 The place→It、my→her 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It is brand-new借走了录音原词 brand-new，可那是 all the appliances are brand-new——全新的是电器，主语是 appliances，不是房子本身；听到 brand-new 就选房子全新，正中圈套。  借用原文：all the appliances are brand-new 

 B) 张冠李戴 It has plenty of rooms近似录音里的 Plenty of space，但那是男方 M 看房后的评价，且说的是"空间大"，并非女方"对房子的陈述"；题干问的是 woman，张冠李戴又偷换了 space→rooms。  借用原文：Plenty of space 

 D) 未提及 It has been vacant for months听上去合理，但全篇没有任何"空置/数月"的信息，女方只说服母亲搬走后"租出去"，并未提空置时长，属凭空添加。

questions.prompt: What is the man's chief consideration in looking for a flat?
options: Space.
Tranquillity.
Appliances.
Location.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the man's chief consideration in looking for a flat? 

 【翻译】 男士在找公寓时首要考虑的是什么? 
 A)  空间。 
 B)  安静。 
 C)  家用电器。 
 D)  位置。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Tranquillity. 
 【定位】 P5 Now, the big question: What about noise and the neighbours? 
 现在，最大的问题是：噪音和邻居怎么样？ 

 【信号】 男方自报"the big question"，强调信号锁定焦点 。答案句靠强调信号定位：男方用 the big question亲手把"噪音和邻居"标成头等大事，紧接第6段女方回答 peaceful pond、tranquility 与之呼应，焦点正是"安静"。 

 【替换】 What about noise and the neighbours? ↔ Tranquillity "不要噪音"概括为"安静"，否定转肯定 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Space借走 Plenty of space，男方确实夸了空间大，但那是顺口称赞，并没被他标成"the big question"，不是"chief"考虑；听到 space 就选，落入只听到原词不分主次的陷阱。  借用原文：Plenty of space 

 C) 原词陷阱 Appliances照搬 all the appliances are brand-new的原词，可那是女方主动介绍的卖点，题干问的是 man's chief consideration，男方并未把电器当首要；既张冠李戴又非"chief"。  借用原文：all the appliances are brand-new 

 D) 过度推断 Location能从 Getting to work was a nightmare联想到位置/通勤，但那是男方吐槽现住处之苦的背景，并非他看这套房时拎出的"the big question"；把背景信息升格成"首要考虑"属过度推断。  借用原文：Getting to work was a nightmare

questions.prompt: What does the man have to do on signing the contract?
options: Talk to his wife about the contract terms.
Pay the first month's rent and a deposit.
Check the references of the flat owner.
Consult his solicitor one more time.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man have to do on signing the contract? 

 【翻译】 男士在签订合同时必须做什么? 
 A)  和妻子谈谈合同条款。 
 B)  支付第一个月的租金和押金。 
 C)  核查公寓房东的资信证明。 
 D)  再咨询一次他的律师。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Pay the first month's rent and a deposit. 
 【定位】 P8 The first month's rent and a deposit are mandatory on signing the contract. 
 签合同时，必须缴纳首月租金和一笔押金。 

 【信号】 mandatory 标出强制动作，触发条件 on signing 对齐 。答案句靠强制信号定位：are mandatory on signing the contract中 mandatory（必须的）直接点出强制要求，且 on signing the contract 与题干触发条件逐字对齐，落点无疑。 

 【替换】 The first month's rent and a deposit are mandatory ↔ Pay the first month's rent and a deposit 名词"是必须的"改写成动词"去支付" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Talk to his wife about the contract terms借了 contract 一词，可录音里男方提妻子是说她上班用车、鞋多，从没说签约时要"和妻子商量合同条款"；听到 contract 就选，正中原词陷阱。  借用原文：as soon as I get a contract drawn up 

 C) 张冠李戴 Check the references of the flat owner盗用 references，但原文是女方说 I spoke to all your references and they all checked out okay——查证明人的是房东、查的是租客；选项把施受方整个调反，且与"签约时"无关。  借用原文：I spoke to all your references and they all checked out okay 

 D) 张冠李戴 Consult his solicitor one more time借走 solicitor，可原文是女方说 as soon as I get a contract drawn up with the solicitor——找律师拟合同的是女方；"男方再咨询一次律师"原文并无，张冠李戴。  借用原文：as soon as I get a contract drawn up with the solicitor

questions.prompt: Why does the man say his wife will feel very excited if they move into the flat?
options: She can have a wonderful view of the pond.
She will be much closer to her work place.
She can make friends with new neighbours.
She will have plenty of space for her shoes.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the man say his wife will feel very excited if they move into the flat? 

 【翻译】 为什么男士说如果他们搬进这套公寓,他的妻子会非常兴奋? 
 A)  她可以欣赏到池塘的美妙景色。 
 B)  她离工作地点会近得多。 
 C)  她可以和新邻居交朋友。 
 D)  她将有足够的空间放她的鞋子。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） She will have plenty of space for her shoes. 
 【定位】 P9 My wife will be thrilled to get out of the shabby place we are now in, and start filling those wardrobes with all those shoes. 
 我妻子一定会兴奋极了，能搬出我们现在这破地方，开始把那些衣柜塞满她所有的鞋子。 

 【信号】 wife 被点名 + thrilled，兴奋理由紧贴其后 。答案句靠"本人被点名 + 情绪词"定位：My wife will be thrilled里 thrilled 正对题干 very excited，其后紧跟的 filling those wardrobes with all those shoes就是兴奋的具体理由——衣柜能装下她所有鞋。 

 【替换】 filling those wardrobes with all those shoes ↔ She will have plenty of space for her shoes "衣柜塞满鞋"概括为"有足够地方放鞋" 
 Lots of closet space too, which is fabulous. My wife has a ridiculous number of shoes ↔ She will have plenty of space for her shoes 前文 closet space + 鞋多，提前埋下"放鞋空间"伏笔 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 She can have a wonderful view of the pond借走原词 pond，录音确有 overlooks a clear and peaceful pond，但那是女方介绍房况，男方说妻子兴奋时绑的是鞋、不是池塘；听到 pond 就选，正中原词陷阱。  借用原文：overlooks a clear and peaceful pond 

 B) 过度推断 She will be much closer to her work place能从 she works nights at the hospital、上班难联想，但原文只说现住处通勤是噩梦，并没说搬进新房"离单位更近"或妻子为此兴奋，属过度推断。  借用原文：she works nights at the hospital 

 C) 未提及 She can make friends with new neighbours借了 neighbours，可原文 all the neighbours are elderly只说邻居都上了年纪、不吵，从没说妻子会"和新邻居交朋友"，纯属添加。  借用原文：all the neighbours are elderly

questions.prompt: What has the new study found about children watching television?
options: The more commercials they see, the more brands they get to know.
The more commercials they see, the more they adore celebrities.
The more television they watch, the fewer conflicts in the family.
The more television they watch, the greater their parents' stress.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has the new study found about children watching television? 

 【翻译】 关于儿童看电视，新研究发现了什么？ 
 A)  他们看的广告越多，了解的品牌就越多。 
 B)  他们看的广告越多，就越崇拜名人。 
 C)  他们看的电视越多，家庭冲突就越少。 
 D)  他们看的电视越多，父母的压力就越大。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The more television they watch, the greater their parents' stress. 
 【定位】 P1 A new study has found a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels. 
 一项新研究发现，孩子看电视的多少与其家长的压力水平之间存在正相关。 

 【信号】 开头点题句即研究结论 。篇章独白常在第一句就抛出研究核心，本段开头 A new study has found a positive correlation 用 "研究发现" 直接报出结论，是典型的开头点题信号，听到 "A new study has found" 就该锁定这句为答案句。 

 【替换】 a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels ↔ The more television they watch, the greater their parents' stress 正相关改写成 "越多越大" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确说看电视越多 the more they're exposed to advertising，但谈的是接触广告进而吵架、增压，并非 "认识更多品牌"；A 借 commercials 这个真出现过的话题词，把结果偷换成认识品牌，是听到原词就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：the more they're exposed to advertising 

 B) 张冠李戴 明星 celebrity endorsements 确在录音里出现，但那是第 4 段讲广告手段时说的，与本题问的 "研究发现" 无关；B 把后文一个原词搬来当本题结论，属张冠李戴式的原词陷阱。  借用原文：celebrity endorsements 

 C) 与原文相反 录音说看电视多会 generate conflict（产生冲突、增加压力），C 却说 "家庭冲突更少"，把录音的因果方向整个反了过来，属与原文相反。  借用原文：This could generate conflict if the parents refuse

questions.prompt: What are parents advised to do to reduce the impact of TV commercials?
options: Inform children of the family's financial situation.
Shift children's attention to interesting activities.
Involve children in making purchasing decisions.
Help children understand advertising's intent.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are parents advised to do to reduce the impact of TV commercials? 

 【翻译】 建议父母做什么来减少电视广告的影响？ 
 A)  告知孩子家庭的财务状况。 
 B)  将孩子的注意力转移到有趣的活动上。 
 C)  让孩子参与购买决策。 
 D)  帮助孩子理解广告的意图。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Involve children in making purchasing decisions. 
 【定位】 P3 The researchers suggest that parents seek input from their children on family purchasing decisions. 
 研究者建议，家长在家庭购买决策上征求孩子的意见。 

 【信号】 建议词 suggest 领出做法 。本句以 The researchers suggest that parents… 开头，suggest 是明确的建议信号词，它后面带出的那个做法就是 "家长被建议做什么" 的答案，听到 suggest 即锁定此句。 

 【替换】 parents seek input from their children on family purchasing decisions ↔ Involve children in making purchasing decisions 征求意见=让孩子参与决策 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音从未让家长告知孩子家庭财务状况，financial situation 在原文找不到对应，属凭常识臆想的未提及项。 
 B) 未提及 录音提到的应对是关掉电视和改变沟通方式，从未说 "把孩子注意力转移到有趣活动上"；interesting activities 是凭空添加，属未提及。 
 D) 原词陷阱 advertising's intent 确在录音出现，但它是第 4 段解释 "孩子为何易受影响" 时说孩子缺乏理解广告意图的认知能力，并非给家长的建议；D 借这个真原词冒充本题答案，是原词陷阱。  借用原文：children don't have the cognitive ability to fully understand advertising's intent

questions.prompt: What makes children particularly vulnerable to TV commercials?
options: Their limited cognitive ability.
Their strong natural curiosity.
Their admiration for celebrities.
Their lack of social experience.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What makes children particularly vulnerable to TV commercials? 

 【翻译】 是什么使儿童特别容易受到电视广告的影响？ 
 A)  他们有限的认知能力。 
 B)  他们强烈的天生好奇心。 
 C)  他们对名人的崇拜。 
 D)  他们缺乏社会经验。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Their limited cognitive ability. 
 【定位】 P4 Plus, children don't have the cognitive ability to fully understand advertising's intent. That makes them particularly vulnerable to advertisements. 
 再加上，孩子不具备充分理解广告意图的认知能力。这使他们特别容易受广告影响。 

 【信号】 That makes them… 收束因果 。末句 That makes them particularly vulnerable 用 "That makes them…" 把前一句的原因（缺乏认知能力）与 "特别易受影响" 的结果直接挂钩，是明确的因果收束信号，听到它就回指前句去找原因。 

 【替换】 children don't have the cognitive ability to fully understand advertising's intent ↔ Their limited cognitive ability "没有充分认知能力"="认知能力有限" 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 录音从未说孩子因 "天生好奇" 而易受影响，natural curiosity 在原文无对应，是凭常识臆测的未提及项。 
 C) 原词陷阱 celebrity endorsements 确在录音里出现，但它是广告吸引孩子的手段之一，不是 "孩子易受影响" 的原因；C 借 celebrities 这个真原词，把广告的手段偷换成孩子的特质，是原词陷阱。  借用原文：celebrity endorsements 

 D) 未提及 录音解释原因时只说孩子缺乏认知能力，从未提 "缺乏社会经验"，social experience 在原文找不到对应，属未提及。

questions.prompt: What baffling phenomenon is discussed in the passage?
options: Bad guys may do good deeds.
Bad guys may go unpunished.
Good guys may not always cooperate.
Good guys may get unfair treatment.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What baffling phenomenon is discussed in the passage? 

 【翻译】 文章讨论了什么令人困惑的现象? 
 A)  坏人可能做好事。 
 B)  坏人可能逃脱惩罚。 
 C)  好人可能并不总是合作。 
 D)  好人可能受到不公平对待。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Good guys may get unfair treatment. 
 【定位】 P1 But sometimes, the good guys also get punished or criticized, specifically because they are so good. 
 但有时候，好人也会仅仅因为他们太好，而恰恰因此受到惩罚或批评。 

 【信号】 转折 But 后才是真意 。前文先说 we do indeed reward good people（确实奖励好人）做铺垫，紧接 But sometimes, the good guys also get punished or criticized 用 But 一转，转折之后才是作者真正要立的反常现象——这句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 the good guys also get punished or criticized ↔ Good guys may get unfair treatment 被罚被批=不公待遇 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项把录音里的 bad guys 搬来拼成「坏人也会做好事」，但录音从没说坏人做好事，只说 we should only punish the bad guys；听到 bad guys 就选会中招。  借用原文：we should only punish the bad guys 

 B) 与原文相反 录音说坏人「会被」惩罚（often punish people who harm others），选项却说坏人「逃脱」惩罚（go unpunished），把极性反了；盗用 punish 一词却改了方向。  借用原文：We also often punish people who harm others 

 C) 张冠李戴 选项说「好人不总愿合作」，盗用了 aren't good team players 里的合作意味，但录音说的是不合作的人会被罚，没说好人不合作；这是把别处的合作话题安到「好人」头上。  借用原文：who aren't good team players

questions.prompt: How are we all judged according to the passage?
options: By what we do.
By fair evaluation.
In comparison with others.
In accordance with set standards.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How are we all judged according to the passage? 

 【翻译】 根据文章,我们所有人是如何被评判的? 
 A)  通过我们所做的事。 
 B)  通过公正的评价。 
 C)  通过与他人比较。 
 D)  根据既定标准。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） In comparison with others. 
 【定位】 P2 After all, we're all judged in comparison with others. 
 毕竟，我们所有人都是在与他人的比较中被评判的。 

 【信号】 judged 原词直接应答 。题干问 how are we judged，录音 we're all judged in comparison with others 里 judged 一词与题干正面咬合，是直接给出依据的应答句；句首 After all（毕竟）是收束总结语气，更确认这是作者下的判定。 

 【替换】 in comparison with others ↔ In comparison with others 近乎原句对应 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 选项「凭我们做什么」看似呼应录音里 stopping that person from looking good 的行为话题，但题干问的是评判依据，录音明说依据是「比较」不是「我们做的事」；用行为话题误导。  借用原文：incentive in stopping that person from looking good 

 B) 未提及 选项「靠公正评价」里的 fair（公正）录音通篇没出现，是凭「评判」话题臆造出的好听说法；录音说的是与人比较，并未强调公正。 
 D) 与原文相反 选项「按固定标准」恰与录音「与他人比较」相对立——录音明确说是相对的比较，不是绝对的标准；这是给出与答案句直接相反的另一极。  借用原文：we're all judged in comparison with others

questions.prompt: What can a normal person do when faced with people who perform better?
options: Learn from them earnestly.
Compete with them actively.
Leave them alone temporarily.
Cooperate with them sincerely.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What can a normal person do when faced with people who perform better? 

 【翻译】 当面对表现更好的人时,普通人能做什么? 
 A)  认真向他们学习。 
 B)  积极与他们竞争。 
 C)  暂时不理会他们。 
 D)  真诚地与他们合作。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Compete with them actively. 
 【定位】 P3 When faced with someone better, what can a normal person do? One option is to actively compete. 
 面对比自己更强的人，一个普通人能做什么呢？一个选择是积极地去竞争。 

 【信号】 设问后第一答 One option 。录音用 what can a normal person do? 自设问，紧接 One option is to actively compete 给出第一个、也是唯一正面的做法；One option 是列举做法的起始信号，作者把「主动竞争」摆在首位，正是答案句。 

 【替换】 One option is to actively compete ↔ Compete with them actively compete/actively 同义重组 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 「向他们认真学习」是面对强者最符合常识的反应，但录音列举的做法里只有竞争和打压，没有 learn；这是用常识替文本，录音根本没念。 
 C) 未提及 「暂时不理他们」录音从未提及，作者给的第二选择是 bring that person down（打压），不是回避；这是凭想象补的做法。  借用原文：A second option is to bring that person down 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项「真诚地与他们合作」盗用了录音里 suppress their cooperation 的 cooperation 一词，但录音说的是「压制别人的合作」，方向恰恰相反，绝非自己去真诚合作。  借用原文：suppress their cooperation or work ethic

questions.prompt: What may discourage people from performing good deeds?
options: Being dismissed as hypocritical.
Not getting the reward they deserve.
Having to make too many sacrifices.
Being misunderstood by people around.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What may discourage people from performing good deeds? 

 【翻译】 什么可能阻碍人们做好事? 
 A)  被当作虚伪而遭到否定。 
 B)  得不到应得的回报。 
 C)  不得不做出太多牺牲。 
 D)  被周围的人误解。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Being dismissed as hypocritical. 
 【定位】 P4 Such good deeds are dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds. This criticism may ultimately discourage people from doing good deeds. 
 这样的善行被那些自己不做这些事的人贬斥为天真或虚伪。这种批评最终可能打消人们行善的念头。 

 【信号】 discourage 前一句即诱因 。题干的 discourage 在 This criticism may ultimately discourage people from doing good deeds 原词复现，而 This criticism 回指上一句 dismissed as naive or hypocritical；指代回指处的那项批评（被斥为伪善）就是打击行善的因素，是答案句。 

 【替换】 dismissed as naive or hypocritical ↔ Being dismissed as hypocritical 近义并保留 hypocritical 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 「得不到应有回报」呼应录音前文 reward good people 的奖励话题，但那是开头铺垫，并非第 4 段 discourage 的诱因；把别段的内容安到本题头上。  借用原文：we do indeed reward good people 

 C) 未提及 「不得不做太多牺牲」录音通篇没提 sacrifice，是对行善代价的常识联想；录音说的打击是被斥伪善，不是牺牲过多。 
 D) 偷换概念 「被周围人误解」听着像 dismissed as hypocritical，但「误解」是中性的认知偏差，录音说的是被恶意贬斥为伪善，程度与性质都不同，属把「被斥伪善」悄悄换成更轻的「被误解」。  借用原文：dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about most preteen children?
options: They are increasingly aware of gender differences.
They engage themselves in positive recollection.
They begin to see the importance of friendship.
They make friends with peers of the same sex.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about most preteen children? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于大多数青春期前儿童说了什么？ 
 A)  他们越来越意识到性别差异。 
 B)  他们进行积极的回忆。 
 C)  他们开始认识到友谊的重要性。 
 D)  他们与同性同龄人交朋友。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They make friends with peers of the same sex. 
 【定位】 P2 Most preteen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age. 
 大多数青春期前的孩子都有一个最好的朋友，这个朋友通常是同性、年龄相仿的。 

 【信号】 总括词most + 段首点题 。这句出现在第二段段首，且以题干同款的 Most preteen children 开头，是讲者对该群体的总括陈述；听到 most 这种总括词紧跟题目所问对象，就该锁定其后内容为答案句。 

 【替换】 a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex ↔ make friends with peers of the same sex have a best friend概括为make friends 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 gender differences 借用了第一段反复出现的 gender differences 一词，但那是讲者引出全文话题的背景，并非对 preteen children 的描述；说 preteen 孩子『越来越意识到性别差异』在该年龄段段落里并无对应。  借用原文：gender differences are very much in the media these days 

 B) 原词陷阱 positive recollection 与录音 positive recollection of these childhood friendships 几乎原词照搬，极具迷惑性；但原文说的是『两性都对这些童年友谊有正面回忆』，主体是回忆童年的成年视角，并非在讲 preteen 孩子当下『正在进行正面回忆』这一行为，答非所问。  借用原文：Both sexes share an essentially positive recollection of these childhood friendships 

 C) 未提及 see the importance of friendship 听上去合情合理，但录音在描述 preteen children 时只说他们有同性好友、玩不同性质的游戏，从未说他们『开始认识到友谊的重要性』，属于无中生有。

questions.prompt: What do most males devote much of their energy to during adolescence?
options: Competing for position.
Forging close ties with friends.
Pursuing fashion.
Fulfilling family obligations.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do most males devote much of their energy to during adolescence? 

 【翻译】 大多数男性在青春期将大部分精力投入到什么上？ 
 A)  争夺地位。 
 B)  与朋友建立亲密关系。 
 C)  追求时尚。 
 D)  履行家庭义务。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Competing for position. 
 【定位】 P4 Now, however, with heightened intensity, considerable energy is devoted to competing for position and a definite undercurrent of competition permeates the relationship. 
 然而此时，随着强度增加，大量精力被投入到争夺地位上，一股明确的竞争暗流贯穿于这段关系之中。 

 【信号】 转折however后 + energy is devoted to原词 。本句以转折词 however 引出青春期男性的真实状态，并直接出现题干同款短语 considerable energy is devoted to competing for position；转折之后才是讲者要强调的结论，加上 devoted to 这一投入信号，定位即落于此。 

 【替换】 considerable energy is devoted to competing for position ↔ Competing for position 几乎原词对应、仅句式调整 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 Forging close ties with friends 借用了同段 a close alliance with same-sex friends，但那是 however 转折之前的铺垫（青春期男性又一次与同性结盟），讲者随即用 however 转折强调真正投入的是竞争；取转折前的信息即答错方向。  借用原文：the majority of males once again report a close alliance with same-sex friends 

 C) 未提及 Pursuing fashion 在整篇录音里没有任何对应，讲者谈的是友谊、竞争、恋爱，从未提及时尚，是凭空添加的干扰项。 
 D) 未提及 Fulfilling family obligations 同样在录音中无对应，讲者讨论的是同伴友谊与竞争，与家庭义务无关，属无中生有。

questions.prompt: What do children do when they reach late adolescence?
options: They prioritize romance over friendship.
They try to strengthen same-sex friendships.
They begin to take friendship more seriously.
They compete intensely for romantic partners.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do children do when they reach late adolescence? 

 【翻译】 儿童在青春期后期会做什么？ 
 A)  他们把恋爱置于友谊之上。 
 B)  他们试图加强同性友谊。 
 C)  他们开始更认真地对待友谊。 
 D)  他们为争夺恋爱对象而激烈竞争。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They prioritize romance over friendship. 
 【定位】 P4 This is most apt to be the case in late adolescence, when dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood. 
 在青春期后期最容易出现这种情况，那时约会和与男生的关系会明显优先于姐妹情谊。 

 【信号】 时间标志late adolescence + 优先级信号take precedence over 。句中 in late adolescence 正是题干同款时间标志，紧跟 take sharp precedence over sisterhood 给出明确的优先级判断；时间标志加『谁优先于谁』信号叠加，即为答案句。 

 【替换】 dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood ↔ prioritize romance over friendship take precedence over等于prioritize over 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 strengthen same-sex friendships 借用了原文反复出现的 same-sex friendships，但本句说的是恋爱『压过』姐妹情、即同性友谊被稀释，并非『加强』；方向恰好相反。  借用原文：dating dilutes the intensity of same sex friendships 

 C) 与原文相反 take friendship more seriously 与录音 take sharp precedence over sisterhood 的取向正相反——原文是恋爱优先、友谊退居其次，而非更看重友谊。  借用原文：dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood 

 D) 原词陷阱 compete intensely for romantic partners 把前文讲青春期男性的 competition 一词移花接木到『争夺恋爱对象』上；原文从未说他们激烈争夺恋爱伴侣，只说恋爱与友谊之间存在竞争，属偷换概念。  借用原文：there's a competition between romance and friendship

questions.prompt: Why do disabled job applicants feel reluctant to disclose their disability information?
options: They regard it as a matter of sheer privacy.
They are worried about being turned down.
They fear that their condition will be made widely known.
They are afraid to be discriminated against once recruited.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why do disabled job applicants feel reluctant to disclose their disability information? 

 【翻译】 为什么残障求职者不愿意披露他们的残障信息? 
 A)  他们认为这纯粹是隐私问题。 
 B)  他们担心会被拒绝。 
 C)  他们害怕自己的状况会被广泛知晓。 
 D)  他们害怕一旦被录用就会受到歧视。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They are worried about being turned down. 
 【定位】 P2 As such, many candidates fear they wouldn't be considered for a position, as a result of disclosing this personal information. 
 正因如此，许多求职者害怕：一旦透露这一个人信息，自己就不会被某职位纳入考虑（即落选）。 

 【信号】 fear + as a result 双重信号 。many candidates fear they wouldn't be considered for a position 中的 fear 直接对应题干的 feel reluctant 的心理，as a result of disclosing 又点出『因披露而……』的因果，这两个信号合起来标定它就是答案句。 

 【替换】 fear they wouldn't be considered for a position ↔ worried about being turned down 怕不被考虑 = 怕被拒 

 【排除】 C) 原词陷阱 录音说的是怕『不被考虑』，并未说怕病情被广泛知晓；C 借 this personal information 这个原词诱你联想到『隐私外泄』，但 made widely known（被广泛传开）是录音没说的内容，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：as a result of disclosing this personal information 

 D) 过度推断 录音的担忧发生在『还没被考虑、怕落选』阶段；D 说 once recruited（一旦被录用后）被歧视，把时间挪到了入职之后，与录音 they wouldn't be considered for a position（怕进不去）方向相反，属过度推断兼时间偷换。  借用原文：they wouldn't be considered for a position 

 A) 未提及 A 说他们把这当作 a matter of sheer privacy（纯属隐私问题），但录音给的理由是『怕落选』这一现实顾虑，并没说他们当作纯隐私来回避，属录音未提及的说法。

questions.prompt: When does the speaker suggest applicants reveal their disability information?
options: After receiving a job offer.
During a job interview.
When confirming an interview.
Upon completing a cover letter.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 When does the speaker suggest applicants reveal their disability information? 

 【翻译】 说话者建议求职者何时披露他们的残障信息? 
 A)  在收到工作邀约之后。 
 B)  在工作面试期间。 
 C)  在确认面试时。 
 D)  在完成求职信时。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） When confirming an interview. 
 【定位】 P3 It's most appropriate to discuss a disability when they reply to confirm an interview. 
 最合适的（披露）时机，是在他们回复确认面试的时候。 

 【信号】 most appropriate 推荐句 。It's most appropriate to discuss a disability when they reply to confirm an interview 用最高级 most appropriate 直接给出『最佳时机』，这种带推荐色彩的句子就是『何时』题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 when they reply to confirm an interview ↔ When confirming an interview 确认面试时 = confirm an interview 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音说的是『确认面试时(confirm an interview)』而非『面试过程中(during)』；B 借 confirm an interview 里的 interview 原词，把时点偷换成 During a job interview，与录音差一个动作环节，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：when they reply to confirm an interview 

 D) 与原文相反 录音明确说残疾信息 needn't be put up front in their cover letter or resumé（不必放进求职信），D 却让人在 completing a cover letter 时披露，正好取了录音否定掉的那个时点，与原文相反。  借用原文：This information needn't be put up front in their cover letter or resumé 

 A) 未提及 A 说在 After receiving a job offer（收到录用通知后）披露，但录音推荐的是确认面试阶段，全篇没说要等到拿 offer 之后，属录音未提及的时点。

questions.prompt: What are people advised to do when filling out their job application form?
options: Describe the true state of their health.
Provide all the information required.
Stress the irrelevance of their disability to the job.
Avoid mentioning the name of their disability.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are people advised to do when filling out their job application form? 

 【翻译】 建议人们在填写求职申请表时做什么? 
 A)  描述他们健康状况的真实情况。 
 B)  提供所有要求的信息。 
 C)  强调他们的残障与工作无关。 
 D)  避免提及他们残障的名称。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Avoid mentioning the name of their disability. 
 【定位】 P4 People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition. 
 人们应当避免说出自己残疾或病症的具体名称。 

 【信号】 should avoid 告诫句 。People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition 用 should avoid 直接给出告诫，这种 should/avoid 的建议措辞就是『建议做什么』题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition ↔ Avoid mentioning the name of their disability 避免说出名称 = avoid mentioning the name 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 让人 Describe the true state of their health（如实描述健康状况），录音却劝人 avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition（避免说出名称），方向正好相反，是与原文相反的干扰。  借用原文：People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition 

 B) 原词陷阱 录音说人们『不应被表格的方式或时机限制』，并未要求 Provide all the information required（提供所有被要求的信息）；B 借录音反复出现的 information 一词诱你选『信息全交』，但全篇恰恰在讲可以有所保留，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：people shouldn't feel restricted by this method or timing 

 C) 未提及 C 让人 Stress the irrelevance of their disability to the job（强调残疾与岗位无关）；录音填表那段只说『避免说出名称』，并未建议在表格里强调残疾与工作无关，属录音未提及的做法。

questions.prompt: What did some American researchers find about students' reading comprehension in the presence of background noise?
options: Their scores were least affected by music with speech.
It was the poorest when there was background speech.
Their scores were most depressed with instrumental music.
It was disrupted by the sound of an air conditioner or fan.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did some American researchers find about students' reading comprehension in the presence of background noise? 

 【翻译】 一些美国研究人员发现,在有背景噪音的情况下,学生的阅读理解能力如何? 
 A)  他们的分数受带有语音的音乐影响最小。 
 B)  当有背景语音时表现最差。 
 C)  他们的分数在有器乐时下降最多。 
 D)  受到空调或风扇声音的干扰。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It was the poorest when there was background speech. 
 【定位】 P2 Students' scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech. Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music than with speech. 
 在有背景人声（说话声）的情况下，学生的成绩下降得最厉害。有音乐时的理解力比有说话声时稍好一些。 

 【信号】 程度极值 most depressed 。答案句靠程度极值信号锁定：scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech 中的 most depressed（下降最厉害）直接回应“成绩最差出现在哪种声音下”，极值词就是听力比较题的落点。 

 【替换】 scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech ↔ It was the poorest when there was background speech most depressed = poorest 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音说有 When the background speech was in a language unfamiliar to participants, there was little if any hindrance，是“陌生语言的人声几乎不干扰”，A 却笼统说成绩受人声影响“最小（least affected）”，偷换并反了极值方向，原文是“最差”才对。  借用原文：there was little if any hindrance of reading comprehension 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音里 most depressed 是接 background speech 的，C 却把 most depressed 安到了 instrumental music 头上。instrumental music 在录音里反而是 Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music，C 盗用了真实出现过的极值词却配错了对象。  借用原文：Students' scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech 

 D) 原词陷阱 air conditioner or fan 确在录音中出现，但那是用来定义 General noise is neutral, such as that from the sound of an air conditioner or fan（举例说明什么叫一般噪音），并非说阅读理解被它“扰乱”，D 借这个原词制造熟耳朵的诱惑，其实答非所问。  借用原文：General noise is neutral, such as that from the sound of an air conditioner or fan

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the British researchers about the degree of interference from background noise?
options: It has to do with the type and volume of the background noise.
It has to do with short-term memory for listening comprehension.
It depends on the overlap in processing different kinds of information.
It depends on the participants' ability to concentrate on the task at hand.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the British researchers about the degree of interference from background noise? 

 【翻译】 从英国研究人员的研究中,我们了解到背景噪音的干扰程度有什么特点? 
 A)  与背景噪音的类型和音量有关。 
 B)  与听力理解的短期记忆有关。 
 C)  取决于处理不同类型信息时的重叠程度。 
 D)  取决于参与者专注于手头任务的能力。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It depends on the overlap in processing different kinds of information. 
 【定位】 P3 It seems the degree of interference from background noise depends on the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise. 
 看来，背景噪音造成的干扰程度，取决于“完成任务所需的信息处理”与“屏蔽背景噪音所需的信息处理”这两者之间的重叠。 

 【信号】 因果信号 depends on 。答案句靠归因信号锁定：depends on the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise 中的 depends on 直接给出“干扰程度由什么决定”，原因题的落点就在 depends on 之后。 

 【替换】 the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise ↔ the overlap in processing different kinds of information 两种处理 = 不同信息处理 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 the type and volume of the background noise 把决定因素说成“噪音的类型和音量”。录音确实念了 background noise，但从没说取决于其 type and volume，volume（音量）更是录音未提，A 借熟词拼了个原文没有的归因。  借用原文：the degree of interference from background noise depends on the overlap 

 B) 原词陷阱 short-term memory 来自录音 British researchers compared the effects… on short-term memory，那是英国研究的“测试对象/实验任务”，B 把它偷换成“干扰程度取决于短期记忆”，张冠李戴。  借用原文：compared the effects of background speech, vocal music, instrumental music, general background noise and silence on short-term memory 

 D) 未提及 the participants' ability to concentrate on the task at hand 听着合理，但英国研究者那段从没说干扰程度取决于“专注能力”，这是录音未提的常识性臆测。

questions.prompt: What is best for students to do when writing essays according to some research?
options: Keep everything as quiet as possible.
Play nothing but instrumental music.
Use vocal material as little as possible.
Wear a pair of earphones or headphones.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is best for students to do when writing essays according to some research? 

 【翻译】 根据一些研究,学生在写论文时最好做什么? 
 A)  尽可能保持一切安静。 
 B)  只播放器乐。 
 C)  尽可能少使用声乐材料。 
 D)  戴一副耳塞或耳机。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Keep everything as quiet as possible. 
 【定位】 P4 When students write essays, however, other research has found it is best to reduce all background noise as much as possible. 
 然而，当学生写作文时，另有研究发现，最好尽可能减少一切背景噪音。 

 【信号】 转折 however + 建议 it is best to 。答案句双信号锁定：转折词 however 提示前面（读书可放纯音乐）之外另起一种场景，紧接的 it is best to reduce all background noise as much as possible 是建议句，转折后的建议正是写作文场景的落点。 

 【替换】 reduce all background noise as much as possible ↔ Keep everything as quiet as possible. 减一切噪音 = 保持安静 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 Play nothing but instrumental music. 里的 instrumental music 来自录音 Instrumental music will have at worst a slight effect，但那是针对“读书/记忆”场景说的；写作文场景明确要求“减少一切噪音”，B 把读书场景的纯音乐建议张冠李戴到写作文上。  借用原文：Instrumental music will have at worst a slight effect 

 C) 原词陷阱 Use vocal material as little as possible. 中 vocal 来自英国研究那段 vocal music was slightly more disruptive than instrumental，写作文场景要求的是“减少一切噪音”而非单单“少用人声”，C 借 vocal 这个原词缩小了范围、答非所问。  借用原文：vocal music was slightly more disruptive than instrumental 

 D) 未提及 Wear a pair of earphones or headphones. 戴耳机听着像隔音的合理办法，但录音从头到尾没提 earphones / headphones，属凭常识臆造。

questions.prompt: How do people of different personalities react to distractions according to other studies?
options: Sociable people were immune to all distractions.
Shy quiet people were most adversely impacted.
Less outgoing people were more affected by silence.
Confident people were unaffected by high-arousal music.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How do people of different personalities react to distractions according to other studies? 

 【翻译】 根据其他研究,不同性格的人对干扰有何反应? 
 A)  善于社交的人对所有干扰都免疫。 
 B)  害羞安静的人受到的不利影响最大。 
 C)  不太外向的人更容易受到安静环境的影响。 
 D)  自信的人不受高兴奋度音乐的影响。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Shy quiet people were most adversely impacted. 
 【定位】 P5 Everyone performed best in the silent condition, but less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions. 
 所有人在安静条件下表现最好，但不那么善于社交（即较内向）的人，受到每一种干扰的负面影响都更大。 

 【信号】 转折 but 后是真意 。答案句靠转折信号锁定：but less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions 中 but 之后才是关于性格差异的真正结论，前半 Everyone performed best in silence 是共性铺垫，转折后才落到“内向者受影响更大”。 

 【替换】 less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions ↔ Shy quiet people were most adversely impacted. less sociable = shy quiet；more affected = most impacted 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 Sociable people were immune to all distractions. 中 sociable 来自录音 less sociable，但录音说外向者“受影响更小”，并未说“对所有干扰免疫”，且 Everyone performed best in the silent condition 表明人人都受干扰（只有安静最好），A 的 immune to all 是绝对化臆断。  借用原文：Everyone performed best in the silent condition 

 C) 与原文相反 Less outgoing people were more affected by silence. 里 Less outgoing 对得上内向者，但录音说大家在 silent condition 下表现最好，内向者是被“各种干扰”影响更大，而非被“安静”影响更大，C 把受影响的对象由 distractions 偷换成 silence，与原文相反。  借用原文：less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions 

 D) 原词陷阱 Confident people were unaffected by high-arousal music. 中 confident、high arousal music 都在录音里出现（subjected shy quiet people and confident outgoing ones to high arousal or low arousal background music），但那只是实验设置，录音没说自信者“不受高唤醒音乐影响”，D 拼接真实原词造了个原文未下的绝对结论。  借用原文：subjected shy quiet people and confident outgoing ones to high arousal or low arousal background music, general noise or silence
